name: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd
title: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd - 500620 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 profit on spot-heavy tanker, LPG and offshore exposure; management gives no earnings outlook, sees crude-tanker order book near 20% with supply arriving CY27-28, and is holding cash rather than buying at current yields.

triggers.quote: Close to all-time highs. No, probably the all-time highs.

triggers.quote: It's just a movement that more of it is available for these large crude tankers.

summary.headline: GE Shipping posts best-ever quarterly profit and first-ever INR1,000 crore annual consolidated net profit, with INR35.10 full-year dividend per share.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the best-ever quarter for profit and FY26 as the best-ever year on consolidated profit, crossing INR1,000 crore net profit for the first time, partly helped by FX movement. Standalone NAV rose to about INR1,422 per share from just over INR1,100 a year earlier, and the company declared its highest-ever quarterly dividend of INR11.70 per share. The Strait of Hormuz closure tightened crude, product and LPG markets in March and April, with spot rates spiking and settling at still-high levels. Management declined to give earnings or quarter-ahead outlook, citing a largely spot-exposed fleet.

financial_highlights.value: Best-ever quarter (figure not stated on call)

financial_highlights.change: Up about INR300 from just over INR1,100 in March 2025; up about INR200 between Dec-25 and Mar-26

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR1,800 (as cited by analyst, not disputed)

financial_highlights.change: To be repaid within about 2 years

segments.name: Crude tankers
segments.commentary: Rates strong from December to February before the Hormuz closure, then spiked in March-April; management says rates have eased from peak but remain very high. Order book about 20%, with supply expected from CY2027-28.

segments.name: Product tankers
segments.commentary: Spiked in March-April and has come off more than crude, though still historically high; management says it is volatile. Order book about 18-22%, roughly in line with crude.

segments.name: LPG carriers
segments.commentary: Rates strong and firming toward quarter end; management says LPG is near all-time highs. Order book about 27%, the heaviest of the segments. All owned LPG ships are on time charter; one is awaiting its next employment and one is due for repricing in coming months.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Unusually strong quarter despite seasonally weak Q1, especially for Capesizes; rates remain firm with coal, iron ore, grains and bauxite cited. Order book about 13%.

segments.name: Offshore support vessels
segments.commentary: Business had its best profit since FY2016, mainly from offshore vessels. About 80-85% of FY27 days covered; some repricings expected later in the year.

segments.name: Offshore drilling (jack-up rigs)
segments.commentary: Simple utilisation includes Middle East standby rigs; marketed utilisation about 84-85%. Three rigs face repricing in FY27, one already idle after a short contract; two come up in 2H FY27. ONGC has cancelled or not processed several tenders, and the company has four rigs, two of them working for non-ONGC clients.

guidance_outlook: No earnings outlook given; management said it does not forecast the market.
About 80% of vessel days for FY27 already locked in.
Time-charter activity expected to stay below 20% of the fleet; management declined to forecast Q1 FY27 numbers.
Asset prices up about 10-20% during the quarter; expected to be volatile.
Replacing older ships through switch transactions will continue; incremental fleet growth at current yields ruled out.
capex_capacity: Switch transactions ongoing: older vessels sold and replaced with newer, similar-type vessels; FY26 purchases were partly timing-driven.
Two in-chartered vessels (one Suezmax crude, one MR product tanker), with 1-3 years remaining; management is open to more in-charter if priced right.
One LPG vessel awaiting delivery to a new charter; floating-rate part-charter on one LPG vessel to start in May 2026.
Yard capacity broadly unchanged; slots for large crude tankers opening up as container and LNG ordering eases.
Jack-up rig newbuilding activity near zero since 2014; management sees no near-term orders.
demand_pricing: Hormuz closure lengthened voyages (ton-miles) as Atlantic Basin and US barrels/LPG replaced Middle East supply; management says this inefficiency has supported rates.
Only about 5% of crude tanker capacity and 2% of product tanker capacity was stuck in the Gulf, though a higher share of cargoes was disrupted.
Two owned/chartered ships were stuck in the Gulf at the time of the call; one owned ship on voyage charter loses revenue while stuck, time-charter ships keep earning.
Time-charter rates for 1-3 year Suezmax and MR vessels moved only a few thousand dollars per day versus spot increases of $30,000-40,000 per day.
Jack-up day rates in Nigeria described as firm; Indian short-term rig rates described as reasonably remunerative but not high.
ONGC rig employment has fallen to one of its lowest levels; an active ONGC tender is ongoing with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: How are day rates trending versus last quarter across tankers and dry bulk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dry bulk and LPG remain very strong, crude has eased but is still strong, and products have eased more; rates settled from March-April spikes but remain historically high.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company locked in time-charter cover after the product tanker spike in April?
qa_highlights.answer: No period fixing was done in March or April because time-charter rates were well below spot; some product coverage exists. Time-charter activity is expected to stay below 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider buybacks now that tax norms have changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one of the biggest impediments has been removed, but any buyback depends on price and is considered when appropriate.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not buy tonnage at current levels for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will replace older ships through switches but will not add incremental tonnage at current yields; it prefers buying at low current yields.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outstanding intercompany loan from GESCO to GIL?
qa_highlights.answer: Two loans: INR65 crore and INR425 crore. Outstanding INR392 crore as of 31 March 2026, plus an old preference share of INR272 crore held by the parent.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash and book breakeven levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash breakeven about $9,000-9,500 per day; book breakeven about $11,000-12,000 per day across the fleet.

risks_watch: Market reversal: spot-heavy fleet is exposed if Hormuz reopens or demand weakens; asset values could fall (management cites a $200 million fleet value drop as absorbable over a year but not within a quarter).
Newbuild supply: crude tanker orderbook built up over the last 3-6 months, with deliveries from CY2027-28.
Indian offshore rig market: ONGC cancellations and delayed tenders; two rigs reprice in 2H FY27.
Possible impairment on vessel switches; management could not quantify.
Trigger for buybacks and larger dividends at a future price level; management says capital allocation is price-dependent.
LPG repricing: one vessel still to be re-chartered, with management declining to say whether rates will exceed prior time-charter levels.
summary.management_tone: Confident on results and the cash position, but evasive on forecasts: management repeatedly declined to give outlook on rates under Hormuz scenarios, Q1 numbers, or buyback pricing, saying the market is guesswork.
key_quotes: this is our best ever quarter in terms of profits. It is also the best ever year in consolidated profits.
For the first time, we crossed INR1,000 crores in consolidated net profit for a year, some of it as a result of the exchange rate movement during the quarter.
we've also declared our highest ever quarterly dividend of INR 11.70 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR35.10 per share.
We don't forecast the market. We have a lot of our capacity on the spot market. So we don't give earnings outlook.
Typically, current yield is a bit of a trap, and we've seen cycles...

adds.what: Switch transactions: older vessels sold and replaced with newer similar-type vessels (no net fleet growth; incremental fleet growth at current yields ruled out)
One LPG vessel awaiting delivery to a new charter
Floating-rate part-charter on one LPG vessel starting May 2026 (in-charter, not owned capacity)

growth.why: No earnings or revenue outlook was given; management declined to forecast Q1 FY27 and said it does not forecast the market. About 80% of FY27 vessel days are locked in and rates remain high, but fleet growth is ruled out, so growth rests on rates and existing contracts rather than new capacity.
